title: Family blames police in man's death: Reject report citing `excited delirium' from mental illness
article: Relatives of a mentally-ill man who died after being pepper sprayed are dismissing a report that rules out the spray as causing his death.
They blame authorities despite the new report from Chief Medical Examiner Graeme Dowling saying that Kasim Cakmak died from "excited delirium due to chronic paranoid schizophrenia."
"Who was giving the pressure?" Cakmak's brother-in-law Sedat Ciplak said. "Who was trying to get him in the handcuffs?
"Just push him on the ground. Two or three guys chasing or wrestling, what's that?"
Ciplak said authorities were badgering Cakmak when he died May 11.
Cakmak, who had schizophrenia, was at the Alberta mental health board's downtown community living program at the time.
He flew into a rage and the Mental Health Crisis Response team was called to take him to Alberta Hospital Edmonton. He became increasingly upset and slapped a nurse.
Two police officers were sent to help in transferring Cakmak, who then became enraged.
He was pepper-sprayed and handcuffed. It was then they noticed he had stopped breathing.
Dowling said that in rare cases some psychiatric patients and people high on cocaine develop excited delirium.
They become aggressive, violent and can develop superhuman strength for no apparent reason. When a person like this is restrained they can stop breathing, he said.
Cakmak emigrated from Turkey in 1990 and didn't speak English well.
Sedat said everyone at the mental health board facility was involved in his brother-in-law's death. He said the family is waiting to hear if there will be a fatality inquiry.
Another family relative, Nebahat Ciplak, said: "Somebody forces you, you get excited. They knew his situation.
"Who caused it? Those policemen. That's my opinion."
She said that when Cakmak would visit her home it would take only a cup of tea and a cigarette to calm him down.
"Maybe if they called one of the family members, they would have come down and helped them out."
